content: HERC5, also known as probable E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase HERC5, is an enzyme encoded by the HERC5 gene in humans. This gene belongs to the HERC family of ubiquitin ligases and produces a protein that contains a HECT (Homologous to the E6-AP Carboxyl Terminus) domain as well as five RCC1 (Regulator of Chromosome Condensation 1) repeats. The expression of the HERC5 gene is upregulated in endothelial cells in response to pro-inflammatory cytokines. The HERC5 protein is primarily localized in the cytoplasm and the perinuclear region of the cell. It functions as an interferon-induced E3 ubiquitin ligase, which plays a critical role in mediating ISGylation, a post-translational modification involving the conjugation of ISG15 (Interferon-Stimulated Gene 15) to target proteins. This modification is part of the cellular antiviral response. The HERC5 gene is located within a cluster of HERC family genes on chromosome 4. Functionally, HERC5 has demonstrated antiviral properties against several pathogens, including HIV-1, influenza A virus, and human papillomavirus (HPV). In terms of protein-protein interactions, HERC5 has been shown to interact with NME2 (Nucleoside Diphosphate Kinase B) and Cyclin E1, suggesting its involvement in diverse cellular processes.
